body.en: A decoder has n input lines and up to 2^n output lines; for each input combination exactly one output is 1. A 2-to-4 decoder has outputs D0 = A1'A0', D1 = A1'A0, D2 = A1A0', D3 = A1A0: each output is one minterm, built with an AND gate (and NOT gates for the complements). An enable input turns the whole decoder on or off. *Decoders* select memory locations and drive seven-segment displays; a 3-to-8 decoder converts binary to octal.

body.en: A multiplexer (MUX, data selector) has 2^n data inputs, n select lines and one output: the select lines choose which data input reaches the output. A 4-to-1 MUX: Y = S1'S0'I0 + S1'S0I1 + S1S0'I2 + S1S0I3. It is built from a 2-to-4 decoder on the select lines ANDed with the data inputs and ORed together. Uses: sharing one line between many signals, and implementing any function of n variables with a 2^n-to-1 MUX. A demultiplexer does the reverse: one input routed to one of many outputs.

explanation.en: A decoder expands a code into one active line; an encoder compresses one active line into a code; a multiplexer chooses one input.

say.en: Sort each description.

tagline.en: Octal-to-binary and decimal-to-BCD encoders, 2-to-4 and 3-to-8 decoders, 4:1 and 8:1 multiplexers, their expressions and their uses.

myth.en: An encoder converts a binary code into one of many output lines, and a decoder converts a key press into a binary code.

truth.en: It is the other way round. An encoder turns one active line into a code (many → few). A decoder turns a code into one active line (few → many). Both words describe a conversion, so they are easy to swap. Think of the TV remote: the keypad encodes your key into a short code, and the TV decodes the code back.

say.en: Encoder: 2^n (or fewer) inputs → n outputs; each output is an OR of inputs.
Decoder: n inputs → 2^n outputs; each output is one minterm (AND gate).
MUX: 2^n data inputs, n select lines, 1 output; it selects one input.
Decimal-to-BCD needs 4 outputs: A3 = D8 + D9, A0 = D1 + D3 + D5 + D7 + D9.

Encoder: many → code. Decoder: code → one of many lines. MUX: many data lines → one output, chosen by select lines.

problem.en: Write the expressions for the outputs of a 3-to-8 decoder with inputs A, B, C (A most significant), and say which output is high for input 101.

steps.en: D0 = A'B'C', D1 = A'B'C, D2 = A'BC', D3 = A'BC
D4 = AB'C', D5 = AB'C, D6 = ABC', D7 = ABC
Input 101 is 5, so only D5 = AB'C is 1.

answer.en: Each Di is minterm mi; for 101 only D5 is high.

D0 equals A'B'C', D1 equals A'B'C, D2 equals A'BC', D3 equals A'BC.
D4 equals AB'C', D5 equals AB'C, D6 equals ABC', D7 equals ABC.
Input 101 is 5, so only D5 equals AB'C is 1.
So the answer is Each Di is minterm mi; for 101 only D5 is high.
